messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — KV cache miss storm detected in us-west1-prod. Rapidly increasing batch sizes + sustained KV writes -> CPU spike and HPA oscillation. Multiple customer errors on text.generate. Root TS: 1845678901
Maya Chen: I'm on pager, taking it. seeing 5x steady-state batch sizes on the runtime metrics dashboard.
Lucas Patel: confirming — queue depth up, continuous batching windows are growing because many prefixes are cold but then hot set expands. KV lookups are exploding.
Maya Chen: customer impact? any 5xxs?
Eli Thompson: ~0.8% 5xx across the cluster last 10m, tail latencies up to 7s for affected shards. Dedicated customers 2 instances reported timeouts.
Sophie Kim: tagging infra: @infra-bot can we temporarily clamp batch.max_tokens or batch.max_size for the affected pool? Need to stop the batch amplification loop.
infra-bot: Suggested mitigation: patch runtime config -> set `batch.max_size: 8` and `batch.max_wait_ms: 30` for pool "inference-runner-usw1". Will apply in canary then prod.
Maya Chen: good. also want to raise HPA minReplicas to avoid flapping while we stabilize. Current HPA min=2, autoscale down to 1 then back up causing warm cache thrash.
Lucas Patel: agree. execute HPA patch to minReplicas=3 for the pool.
Maya Chen: applying hotfix:
```
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-runner-usw1 --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3}}'
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/inference-runner --env="BATCH_MAX_SIZE=8" --record
```
Maya Chen: rolling patch to 2 pods first as canary. watching metrics.
Sophie Kim: also reducing `kv.write_backoff_ms` to slow writes; the write fanout is part of the blowup. Suggest `kv.write_backoff_ms: 50` -> 200ms.
Eli Thompson: note: if we throttle writes too hard, customers with heavy stateful workloads may see increased latency. we should communicate before broad change.
Lucas Patel: can we do targeted config for the public hosted pool only? keep dedicated customers untouched for now.
Maya Chen: doing targeted config on "hosted-usw1" pool only.
infra-bot: Applying config on pool hosted-usw1 -> `batch.max_size=8`, `kv.write_backoff_ms=200`, `kv.cache_ttl=45s`. Canaries: 2 pods -> 10 pods -> full rollout.
incident-bot: Noted deployment: config-hotfix/1845678901 initiated. Observability: track `batch_size.p50/p95`, `kv.miss_rate`, `hpa.replica_count`.
Maya Chen: after canary: batch sizes dropped from median 40 -> 6, cpu per pod down 42% -> 15%. latency p95 from 4.9s -> 1.2s.
Eli Thompson: error rate fell to 0.15% in canary. but we're seeing a slower secondary bump in misses as caches warm -> could cause another wave.
Sophie Kim: we need a plan to prevent re-trigger: consider sticky prefix caching and a gradual warmup when bringing replicas up. HPA scale-up should prefer warm-up pods.
Lucas Patel: proposal: add a warmup label to new pods and route 20% of traffic to warmup pool with `batch.max_size=4` and pre-populate KV for top prefixes. then move traffic over 10m.
Maya Chen: good. also add a short-term scaling cooldown on HPA: `behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` to avoid immediate scale down/up thrash.
Eli Thompson: I'll open quick PR for HPA behavior changes and submit for fast-merge.
Sophie Kim: customer comms POV: send short note to affected customers saying we're mitigating a KV/cache-induced latency spike; remediation applied; follow-up full postmortem later. Prod support draft ready?
Maya Chen: drafting now, will ping support to send.
infra-bot: Hotfix rollout progressed: canary -> 25% -> 100% over 18 minutes. No regressions noted. Metrics: stable.
Maya Chen: bumping this to 'monitoring' in incident tracker. handing to Sophie for 8h oncall to run the follow-up (harden HPA + warmup strategy).
Sophie Kim: taking handoff. I have runbook steps and checklist:
- confirm HPA stabilization window set
- implement warmup label and traffic split
- add KV key prefetch for top 100 prefixes
- schedule postmortem and RCA owner
- prepare rollback plan for config changes
Maya Chen: thx. leaving notes in the incident doc: https://redwood/internal/incidents/1845678901
Sophie Kim: noted. adding owner for RCA: Lucas.
Lucas Patel: will lead RCA, initial hypothesis: cache write amplification + permissive batching growth + aggressive HPA cooldowns. follow-up to include load repro and perf test.
Eli Thompson: I'll collect heap snapshots and histograms for the affected pods, attach to incident doc.
Sophie Kim: closing pager for Maya — marked stable. ongoing action items assigned.
incident-bot: Incident transition: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared for primary oncall.
Maya Chen: thanks team, handoff complete.
Sophie Kim: will update when RCA timeline and postmortem are ready.
infra-bot: Automated note: consider adding a guard in runtime: `if batch.size > 16 then clamped=true and rate_limit=true` as a safety valve. filing infra ticket INF-4291.
